weeks.title: Thinking at the Margin: Scarcity, Trade-offs and Business Choices
weeks.summary: Is week aap scarcity, opportunity cost, sunk cost aur marginal analysis ko business data ke saath use karna seekhoge, taaki 'aur ek unit / aur ek rupaya lagayein ya nahi' jaise decisions numbers se le sako.
concepts: **Scarcity**: har business ke resources limited hote hain: budget, shelf space, warehouse capacity, machine hours, aur analyst ke ghante bhi. Isliye har decision ek **trade-off** hai: ek cheez chunne ka matlab doosri chhodna. Data analyst ka kaam aksar yahi hai ki is trade-off ko numbers mein dikhaye.

**Opportunity cost**: kisi choice ki asli cost = sabse achha agla alternative jo chhoda gaya (next best alternative), saare chhode gaye alternatives ka sum nahi. Isme **explicit cost** (cash jo diya) aur **implicit cost** (apne resource ka chhoda hua return, jaise founder ki chhodi hui salary) dono aate hain.

**Sunk cost**: jo paisa pehle kharch ho chuka aur kisi bhi decision se wapas nahi aayega (non-refundable research fee, purana ad campaign). Rational decision mein sunk cost **ignore** hota hai; sirf woh revenue aur cost compare karo jo is decision se badlenge (**incremental / relevant** items). 'Itna lag gaya hai, ab rok nahi sakte' wali soch ko sunk cost fallacy kehte hain.

**Marginal analysis**: decision 'kitna' ka ho to ek-ek extra unit dekho. **Marginal benefit (MB)** = ek extra unit se total benefit kitna badha; **marginal cost (MC)** = total cost kitna badha. Rule: jab tak MB ≥ MC hai, activity badhao; jahan MB < MC ho jaaye wahan ruko. Isi point par total net benefit maximum hota hai.

**Diminishing marginal returns**: zyada tar real data mein har extra input ka extra output ghat-ta jaata hai: pehle ₹10,000 ke ads se 400 orders, agle ₹10,000 se sirf 300. Isliye **average** (total ÷ units) aur **marginal** alag hote hain; average achha dikh sakta hai jabki aakhri unit loss de rahi ho.

**Marginal vs average cost**: ek extra order accept karna hai ya nahi, ye average cost se nahi, marginal cost se decide hota hai. Agar fixed cost pehle se lag chuki hai to extra order ko sirf apni extra cost cover karni hai. Average cost se kam price wala order bhi profit badha sakta hai.

**Analyst ka toolkit**: data ko 'cumulative' se 'incremental' mein convert karo (har row ka difference lo), har step ka MB aur MC ek table mein rakho, aur sunk ya allocated fixed costs ko alag column mein mark karke decision se bahar rakho. Yahi logic aage break-even, pricing aur A/B test ke analysis mein baar-baar aayega.

example.problem: Fictional cloud kitchen 'Tadka Junction' online ads par ₹10,000 ke blocks mein kharch karta hai. Data: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 blocks par total orders 400, 700, 900, 1,000, 1,050 aate hain. Har order se ₹80 contribution (price − food aur packaging cost) milta hai. Kitne blocks chalane chahiye?
steps: Cumulative orders ko marginal mein badlo: 400, 300, 200, 100, 50 extra orders per block.
Har block ka marginal benefit = extra orders × ₹80: ₹32,000, ₹24,000, ₹16,000, ₹8,000, ₹4,000.
Har block ka marginal cost = ₹10,000.
Block 1, 2, 3 mein MB > MC hai (₹32,000, ₹24,000, ₹16,000 sab ₹10,000 se zyada). Block 4 ka MB ₹8,000 < ₹10,000, to woh loss deta hai.
Check: net profit (contribution − ad spend) 1 se 5 blocks par ₹22,000, ₹36,000, ₹42,000, ₹40,000, ₹34,000 hai; maximum 3 par.
Trap: 5 blocks par average contribution per block ₹84,000 ÷ 5 = ₹16,800 bhi ₹10,000 se zyada hai, par ye average hai; aakhri do blocks ka marginal benefit cost se kam hai.
Answer: **3 blocks (₹30,000) chalao**, net profit ₹42,000.

mistakes: Opportunity cost mein saare chhode gaye options jod dena. Sirf next best alternative ki value lo, kyunki ek saath sab alternatives kabhi mil hi nahi sakte the.
Sunk cost ko decision mein ghusaana, jaise 'research par ₹4 lakh lag chuke hain, isliye launch karna hi padega'. Fix: sirf future incremental revenue aur cost compare karo.
Average numbers se 'aur badhao' decide karna. Average positive hone par bhi marginal unit loss de sakti hai; hamesha cumulative data ka difference lekar marginal column banao.
revision: Opportunity cost = next best alternative ki value (explicit + implicit).
Sunk cost ignore; sirf incremental revenue aur cost relevant hain.
Activity tab tak badhao jab tak MB ≥ MC; MB < MC par ruko.
Marginal = cumulative ka difference; average aur marginal alag hote hain.
Extra order ka decision marginal cost se, average cost se nahi.

questions.question: Fictional 'Sutra Stores' ke paas ek khaali shelf hai. Teen options hain: snacks (₹12,000 per month profit), stationery (₹9,000 per month) ya phone accessories (₹15,000 per month). Store phone accessories chunta hai. Is choice ki opportunity cost kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost sirf next best alternative ki value hai. Phone accessories ke baad sabse achha option snacks hai (₹12,000), isliye option B sahi hai. Option A (₹12,000 + ₹9,000) saare chhode gaye options jodne ka trap hai; ek shelf par dono ek saath nahi aa sakte the. Option D chuni hui cheez ka apna profit hai, cost nahi.

questions.question: Fictional 'Megha Foods' ek naye snack ki market research par ₹4 lakh kharch kar chuki hai; ye paisa kisi bhi haal mein wapas nahi milega. Ab decide karna hai ki snack launch karein ya nahi. Is decision mein ₹4 lakh ko kaise treat karna chahiye?
options: Launch ke expected cost mein jodna chahiye
Launch zaroor karna chahiye, warna ₹4 lakh waste ho jaayenge
Launch tabhi karo jab expected profit pehle ₹4 lakh recover kar sake
Ignore karna chahiye; sirf launch se aane wale future revenue aur cost compare karo
questions.explanation: ₹4 lakh sunk cost hai: launch karo ya na karo, ye wapas nahi aayega, isliye dono choices mein same hai aur decision ko nahi badalta. Option D sahi hai. Options B aur C sunk cost fallacy ke do roop hain (paisa 'bachaane' ke liye ya 'recover' karne ke liye decision badalna). Option A ise future cost samajhne ki galti hai.

questions.question: Fictional factory 'Ankur Plastics' ke paas ek overtime shift ka option hai: 500 extra bottles banengi jo ₹40 each mein bikengi. Har bottle ka material cost ₹22 hai aur shift ke liye overtime wages ₹6,000 lagenge. Factory ka monthly rent ₹50,000 hai jo pehle se fixed hai. Overtime shift se profit kitna badhega?
questions.explanation: Incremental revenue = 500 × ₹40 = ₹20,000. Incremental cost = 500 × ₹22 + ₹6,000 = ₹17,000. Profit ₹3,000 badhega, option A. Rent shift ho ya na ho, same rehta hai, isliye irrelevant hai; use ghataane se option C (−₹47,000) aata hai. Option B overtime wages bhoolne ka trap hai, aur option D material cost bhoolne ka.

questions.question: Fictional 'Rasta Couriers' har mahine 1,000 deliveries karta hai; total cost ₹60,000 hai (average ₹60 per delivery). Analyst ke cost model ke hisaab se 1,100 deliveries par total cost ₹64,500 hogi. Ek B2B client 100 extra deliveries ₹50 each par maangta hai, aur iska baaki business par koi asar nahi. Sahi decision kya hai?
options: Reject; ₹50 average cost ₹60 se kam hai, har delivery par ₹10 ka loss
Reject; is order par kul ₹1,000 ka loss hoga
Accept; extra delivery ka marginal cost ₹45 hai, profit ₹500 badhega
questions.explanation: Marginal cost = (₹64,500 − ₹60,000) ÷ 100 = ₹45 per delivery. Extra revenue ₹5,000 − extra cost ₹4,500 = ₹500 profit, isliye option C. Options A aur B average cost (₹60) se compare karne ka trap hain; fixed cost pehle se lag chuki hai, extra order ko sirf apni extra cost cover karni hai. Option D extra cost ko bilkul ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Fictional grocery app 'Jaldi Mart' ke ek zone mein delivery riders ki sankhya ke hisaab se monthly contribution (₹ hazaar mein): 1 rider: 40, 2 riders: 75, 3 riders: 100, 4 riders: 115, 5 riders: 125. Har rider ka cost ₹18 hazaar per month hai. Profit maximise karne ke liye kitne riders rakhne chahiye?
questions.explanation: Marginal contribution: 40, 35, 25, 15, 10 (₹ hazaar). Rider tab tak add karo jab tak MB ≥ MC (18). Teesre rider ka MB 25 > 18 hai, chauthe ka 15 < 18, isliye 3 riders, option D. Check: profit = 22, 39, 46, 43, 35, maximum 3 par. Option A total contribution maximise karne ka trap hai (cost bhool gaye). Option B 'pehle rider ka return sabse zyada hai' wali galti hai.

questions.question: Fictional fashion brand 'Rang Rasiya' ne ek season ke kurtas ₹2,00,000 mein banwaaye the jo nahi bike. Ab do options hain: (i) jaise hain waise ek outlet ko ₹90,000 mein bech do, ya (ii) ₹40,000 lagakar redesign (rework) karo aur ₹1,50,000 mein becho. Sahi decision aur uska reason kya hai?
options: Rework karo; as-is bechne se ₹20,000 zyada milega
As-is becho; rework par ₹40,000 aur lagaana nuksaan ke upar nuksaan hai
Rework karo; as-is bechne se ₹60,000 zyada milega
Koi farak nahi; dono mein ₹2,00,000 to doob hi chuka hai
questions.explanation: ₹2,00,000 sunk hai, dono options mein same. Incremental comparison: rework net = ₹1,50,000 − ₹40,000 = ₹1,10,000; as-is = ₹90,000. Rework ₹20,000 behtar hai, option A. Option C rework cost ghataana bhool jaata hai (₹1,50,000 − ₹90,000). Option D sahi pehchaanta hai ki ₹2,00,000 sunk hai, par phir future cash flows compare karna bhool jaata hai. Option B extra kharch ko automatically bura maan leta hai bina incremental return dekhe.

weeks.title: Demand, Supply and Price Elasticity in Pricing Decisions
weeks.summary: Is week aap demand aur supply curves, equilibrium, aur price/income/cross elasticity ko sales data se nikaalna seekhoge, aur samjhoge ki price badalne par revenue kab badhta hai aur kab ghatta hai.
concepts: **Demand function**: price aur quantity demanded ka relation, jaise Qd = a − bP. Price badalne par curve ke **along movement** hota hai. Baaki factors (income, substitutes/complements ki price, taste, expectations, buyers ki sankhya) badlein to poori curve **shift** hoti hai: right = har price par zyada demand.

**Supply aur equilibrium**: supply curve (Qs = c + dP) input cost, technology, sellers ki sankhya se shift hoti hai. Equilibrium par Qd = Qs. Price equilibrium se neeche atak jaaye (cap) to **shortage** = Qd − Qs; upar atak jaaye to **surplus** = Qs − Qd.

**Price elasticity of demand (PED)**: e = %ΔQ ÷ %ΔP, demand ke liye negative hota hai, isliye aksar |e| bolte hain. |e| > 1 elastic, |e| < 1 inelastic, |e| = 1 unit elastic. Do data points ke beech **midpoint (arc) method** use karo: %ΔQ = ΔQ ÷ average Q, %ΔP = ΔP ÷ average P, taaki upar ya neeche jaane par same answer aaye.

**Point elasticity** linear demand Q = a − bP par: e = −b × P ÷ Q. Ek hi line par elasticity har point par alag hai: upar (high price, low Q) elastic, neeche inelastic. Isliye 'is product ki elasticity −1.2 hai' kehte waqt price level bhi batana chahiye.

**Elasticity aur revenue**: elastic range mein price cut se total revenue (P × Q) badhta hai, inelastic range mein price badhaane se. Linear demand Q = a − bP par revenue maximum P = a ÷ 2b par hota hai, jahan |e| = 1. Dhyaan do: revenue maximum hona profit maximum hona nahi hai; profit ke liye cost bhi chahiye.

**Income aur cross elasticity**: income elasticity = %ΔQ ÷ %Δincome (positive = normal good, negative = inferior). Cross-price elasticity = %ΔQ(X) ÷ %ΔP(Y): positive = substitutes (do competing chai brands), negative = complements (printer aur cartridge). Category managers isse cannibalisation aur bundle decisions lete hain.

**Supply elasticity**: %ΔQs ÷ %ΔP. Short run mein supply aksar inelastic hoti hai (capacity fixed), long run mein zyada elastic. Perishable ya capacity-constrained products (hotel rooms, flights) mein price spikes isi wajah se aate hain.

**Analyst ka tareeka**: past price changes ya A/B price tests ke data se elasticity estimate karte hain. Ek common model hai ln Q = α + β ln P; yahan slope β seedha elasticity hai (constant-elasticity demand). Dhyaan rakho ki price ke saath season, promotion ya competitor price bhi na badle ho, warna estimate biased hoga.

example.problem: Fictional 'Kesar Dairy' ke analyst ne flavoured milk ki daily demand estimate ki: Q = 5,000 − 100P (P ₹ mein, Q bottles). Abhi price ₹20 hai. Elasticity nikaalo, batao price badhaana revenue ke liye theek hai ya nahi, aur revenue-maximising price kya hai.
steps: Point elasticity e = −b × P ÷ Q = −100 × 20 ÷ 3,000 = −0.67. |e| < 1, yaani demand inelastic hai.
Inelastic range mein price badhaane se quantity proportionally kam girti hai, isliye revenue badhega.
Revenue-maximising price = a ÷ 2b = 5,000 ÷ 200 = ₹25.
P = 25 par Q = 2,500 aur revenue = ₹62,500, jo ₹60,000 se zyada hai; yahan |e| = 100 × 25 ÷ 2,500 = 1.
Answer: |e| ≈ **0.67 (inelastic)**, price badhaana revenue badhayega, aur revenue **₹25 par maximum (₹62,500)** hai. Profit decision ke liye per-bottle cost bhi dekhna padega.

mistakes: Simple % change (base value se) use karna; upar aur neeche jaane par alag elasticity aati hai. Do points ke beech midpoint method use karo.
Ek linear demand curve ki ek hi elasticity maan lena. Point elasticity −b × P ÷ Q har price par badalti hai.
Revenue-maximising price ko profit-maximising maan lena. Variable cost zero na ho to profit-maximising price revenue-maximising price se upar hota hai.
revision: Price change: curve ke along movement; doosre factors: curve shift.
Shortage = Qd − Qs (price cap equilibrium se neeche).
Midpoint: %Δ = change ÷ average; point: e = −b × P ÷ Q.
Elastic: price cut se revenue badhta hai; inelastic: price rise se.
Linear demand: revenue max at P = a ÷ 2b, jahan |e| = 1.
Cross elasticity positive = substitutes, negative = complements.

questions.question: Mobile data packs ki price kaafi gir jaati hai. OTT streaming subscriptions (jo data ke saath use hoti hain, yaani complement) ke market mein kya hoga?
options: Streaming ki demand curve left shift hogi
Streaming ki supply curve right shift hogi
Streaming ki demand curve right shift hogi
Streaming ki demand curve ke along neeche movement hoga
questions.explanation: Complement (data) sasta hone par har streaming price par zyada log subscribe karenge, isliye streaming ki demand curve right shift hoti hai, option C. Option D trap hai: curve ke along movement sirf streaming ki apni price badalne par hota hai. Option A substitutes ke liye hota. Supply side (option B) par data price ka seedha asar nahi.

questions.question: Sales data se analyst dekhta hai ki jab fictional tea brand 'Pahadi Leaf' ne price 10% badhaayi, to competing brand 'Neel Giri' ki sales 6% badh gayi (baaki sab same). Cross-price elasticity aur dono brands ka relation kya hai?
questions.explanation: Cross-price elasticity = %ΔQ(Neel Giri) ÷ %ΔP(Pahadi Leaf) = +6% ÷ +10% = +0.6. Positive sign ka matlab substitutes, option A. Option D ratio ulta lene ka trap hai (10 ÷ 6). Option C number sahi par sign ka matlab galat padhta hai; complements ke liye sign negative hota.

questions.question: Ek fictional city market mein ek cooking gas accessory ki demand Qd = 900 − 15P aur supply Qs = 25P − 300 hai (P ₹ mein). Ek bada platform price ₹24 par cap kar deta hai. Is price par market mein kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Equilibrium: 900 − 15P = 25P − 300 ⇒ P = 30, Q = 450. ₹24 equilibrium se neeche hai, to Qd = 900 − 360 = 540 aur Qs = 600 − 300 = 300; shortage = 540 − 300 = 240, option D. Option B (540 − 450) aur option C (450 − 300) dono equilibrium quantity se compare karne ka trap hain; shortage Qd aur Qs ka gap hai. Option A cap ko floor samajhne ki galti hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Chhaya Umbrellas' ka estimated demand Q = 1,200 − 40P hai. Abhi price ₹18 hai. Is price par point elasticity aur pricing implication kya hai?
options: |e| = 0.67, inelastic; price cut se revenue ghatega
|e| = 1.5, elastic; chhota price cut revenue badhayega
|e| = 1.5, elastic; price badhaane se revenue badhega
|e| = 1, unit elastic; chhote price change se revenue nahi badlega
questions.explanation: Q = 1,200 − 40 × 18 = 480. e = −40 × 18 ÷ 480 = −1.5, to |e| = 1.5, elastic. Elastic range mein price cut se quantity proportionally zyada badhti hai, isliye revenue badhta hai, option B. Option C elasticity sahi nikaalta hai par revenue rule ulta lagata hai. Option A ratio ulta lene (480 ÷ (40 × 18)) ka trap hai.

questions.question: Fictional ed-tech app 'Vidya Plus' ne A/B price test kiya: ₹199 per month par 5,000 subscriptions aur ₹249 par 4,200. Midpoint method se price elasticity (absolute value) kitni hai, aur revenue ka kya hua?
questions.explanation: %ΔQ = −800 ÷ 4,600 = −17.4%; %ΔP = 50 ÷ 224 = 22.3%; |e| = 17.4 ÷ 22.3 ≈ 0.78 (inelastic). Revenue ₹9,95,000 se ₹10,45,800 hua, yaani badha, option A. Option B base values se simple % lene ka result hai (16% ÷ 25.1%). Option C ratio ulta hai. Option D elasticity sahi rakh kar inelastic demand mein price rise ka revenue effect ulta samajhta hai.

questions.question: Fictional bakery chain 'Mithas' ke data ke hisaab se ek cake ki weekly demand linear hai: ₹30 par 1,100 units bikti hain aur ₹45 par 800 units. Kis price par weekly revenue maximum hoga?
questions.explanation: Slope b = (1,100 − 800) ÷ (45 − 30) = 20 units per ₹. Q = 1,100 − 20(P − 30) = 1,700 − 20P. Revenue maximum P = a ÷ 2b = 1,700 ÷ 40 = ₹42.50 (Q = 850, revenue ₹36,125), option D. Option B choke price (Q = 0) hai, jahan revenue zero hai. Options A aur C sirf diye gaye data points mein se behtar wala chunne ka trap hain; ₹45 par revenue ₹36,000 hai, jo ₹36,125 se kam hai.

weeks.title: Business Markets: B2C vs B2B, Services and How Organisations Buy
weeks.summary: Is week aap B2C aur B2B markets ka farak, services ki khaas properties, organisational buying behaviour, buying situations aur decision-making unit samjhoge, aur dekhoge ki B2B data (account value, order patterns) analyst kaise padhta hai.
concepts: **B2C vs B2B**: B2C mein bahut saare chhote buyers, chhota ticket size, emotion aur brand ka bada role, aur purchase jaldi hota hai. B2B mein kam par bade buyers, professional purchasing, formal process (RFQ, tender, contract), lamba sales cycle, aur relationship + technical specs ka bada role. Analyst ke liye: B2B mein ek account ka loss poore quarter ka revenue hila sakta hai, isliye account-level data (orders, renewals, contacts) zyada important hai.

**Derived demand aur volatility**: B2B demand end-consumer demand se nikalti hai: cartons ki demand snacks ki sales par depend karti hai. Beech ke distributors inventory rules follow karte hain, isliye consumer demand mein chhota badlaav upstream orders mein bada swing banata hai (**bullwhip effect**). B2B forecasting mein isliye customer ke customer ka data bhi dekhna padta hai.

**Services ki properties (IHIP)**: **intangibility** (chhoo nahi sakte, isliye trust aur evidence chahiye), **inseparability** (production aur consumption saath, customer process ka hissa), **heterogeneity/variability** (har baar quality thodi alag, isliye standard process aur metrics), **perishability** (aaj ki khaali hotel room ya flight seat kal nahi bik sakti, isliye capacity utilisation aur dynamic pricing).

**Organisational buying behaviour**: company ka decision chaar levels ke factors se banta hai: environmental (economy, regulation, technology), organisational (policies, budget cycle, purchase process, centralised vs decentralised buying), interpersonal (buying team ke andar authority aur persuasion) aur individual (har member ki age, risk appetite, incentives). Formal process: need recognition → specification → supplier search → proposals → selection → order routine → performance review.

**Buying situations**: **straight rebuy** (same item, same supplier, routine reorder, aksar automatic PO), **modified rebuy** (specs, price ya supplier badalna hai, thodi research), **new task** (pehli baar khareed, zyada risk, bada buying team, sabse lamba process). In-supplier ka goal rebuy ko routine rakhna hai; out-supplier modified rebuy ke mauke dhoondhta hai.

**Decision-making unit (DMU / buying centre)**: initiator (zaroorat pehchaanta hai), user (product use karega), influencer (specs aur evaluation mein input, jaise IT ya finance), decider (final choice), approver (decision authorise karta hai), buyer (supplier se terms aur order) aur **gatekeeper** (information flow control karta hai, jaise purchase assistant jo decide kare kaunse vendors team tak pahunchein). Ek insaan kai roles le sakta hai.

**Sales techniques**: transactional selling price aur product par focus karta hai; **consultative selling** customer ki problem samajh kar solution design karta hai. **SPIN** questioning: Situation (current setup ke facts), Problem (pain points), Implication (problem ka business impact), Need-payoff (solution ki value customer khud bole). B2B mein value numbers mein dikhani padti hai (downtime cost, savings), yahin analyst kaam aata hai.

**Account value**: B2B account ki value ek order se nahi, poore relationship se judge karo: annual margin × expected relationship length (simple version), ya retention probability ke saath expected value. Agar har saal account rehne ki probability r hai aur pehle saal ka margin pakka hai, to expected total margin = m × (1 + r + r² + ...) = m ÷ (1 − r) (discounting ignore karke).

example.problem: Fictional hospital chain 'Arogya Hospitals' pehli baar patient-flow analytics platform khareed rahi hai. Operations head ne problem uthaayi, nurses aur front desk platform use karenge, IT head security specs likhta hai, COO vendor chunega, CFO budget sign karta hai, aur procurement manager contract negotiate karega. Buying situation aur DMU roles batao, aur vendor ke liye account value nikaalo agar contract ₹24 lakh per saal, vendor ka gross margin 40% aur expected relationship 5 saal hai.
steps: Pehli baar khareed, naya category, high risk: buying situation **new task** hai.
Operations head = initiator; nurses aur front desk = users; IT head = influencer (specs).
COO = decider; CFO = approver; procurement manager = buyer.
Vendor ko IT head aur CFO ke liye alag evidence chahiye: security compliance aur ROI numbers.
Annual margin = ₹24 lakh × 40% = ₹9.6 lakh.
5 saal ka margin (discounting ignore) = ₹9.6 lakh × 5 = ₹48 lakh.
Answer: **new task**, DMU roles upar jaise, aur account value lagbhag **₹48 lakh margin**, isliye vendor ke liye lamba sales effort justify hota hai.

mistakes: B2B order data ko B2C jaisa treat karna: har order ko independent maan lena. B2B mein orders inventory rules aur contracts se aate hain, isliye bullwhip aur account-level patterns dekho.
DMU mein sirf 'jo cheque sign karta hai' us par focus karna. Influencers aur gatekeepers deal ko pehle hi rok sakte hain; har role ki zaroorat alag se address karo.
Account value ek saal ke revenue se judge karna. Revenue nahi, margin lo, aur relationship length ya retention probability shaamil karo.
revision: B2B: kam aur bade buyers, derived demand, formal process, lamba cycle.
IHIP: intangibility, inseparability, heterogeneity, perishability.
Straight rebuy → modified rebuy → new task: risk aur effort badhta hai.
DMU: initiator, user, influencer, decider, approver, buyer, gatekeeper.
SPIN: Situation, Problem, Implication, Need-payoff.
Expected margin with retention r: m ÷ (1 − r).

questions.question: Fictional factory 'Vega Auto Parts' ka ERP har mahine same supplier se same grade ka lubricant oil automatically reorder karta hai, bina kisi review ke. Ye kaunsi buying situation hai?
questions.explanation: Same item, same supplier, routine aur bina review ke reorder: straight rebuy, option A. Option B tab hota jab specs, price ya supplier badalne par vichaar hota. Option C pehli baar ki khareed hai. Option D ek poora integrated solution ek supplier se lene ko kehte hain, jo yahan nahi hai.

questions.question: Fictional hotel 'Sagar Inn' ke 20 rooms aaj raat khaali reh gaye. Kal in rooms ko 'aaj ki raat' ke liye bechna possible nahi hai. Service ki kaunsi property yahan dikh rahi hai?
questions.explanation: Service store nahi ho sakti: aaj ki khaali capacity hamesha ke liye chali gayi. Ye perishability hai, option C, aur isi wajah se hotels dynamic pricing aur overbooking use karte hain. Option A (chhoo na paana) aur option D (quality mein variation) bhi services ki properties hain par is situation ko describe nahi karti.

questions.question: Fictional company 'Lohit Steel' mein purchase department ka ek executive decide karta hai ki kaunse vendors ke brochures, emails aur meeting requests engineering team tak pahunchein aur kaunse nahi. Buying centre mein uska role kya hai?
questions.explanation: Jo vyakti buying team tak information aur vendors ki pahunch control kare, woh gatekeeper hai, option B. Influencer (option A) specs ya evaluation par input deta hai, jaise engineers ya IT head; yahan executive kuch evaluate nahi kar raha, sirf flow rok ya aage bhej raha hai. Decider final choice karta hai, user product use karta hai.

questions.question: Ek fictional distributor apna inventory hamesha agle 2 mahine ki sales ke barabar rakhta hai (sales = pichhle mahine ki sales). Pichhle mahine sales 1,000 units thi, inventory 2,000 units, aur woh har mahine 1,000 units order karta tha. Is mahine sales 10% badh kar 1,100 ho gayi. Is mahine distributor manufacturer ko kitna order dega?
questions.explanation: Order = bechi gayi units ki bharpaai + inventory target ka badlaav. Target inventory 2 × 1,100 = 2,200 hai, yaani 200 badha. Order = 1,100 + 200 = 1,300, jo 1,000 se 30% zyada hai, option D. Consumer demand 10% badhi par manufacturer ke order 30%: yahi bullwhip effect hai. Option A inventory adjustment bhool jaata hai; option C naye target inventory ko hi order samajhta hai.

questions.question: Ek predictive-maintenance software ka salesperson plant manager se poochta hai: "Agar ye unplanned breakdowns isi tarah mahine mein do baar hote rahe, to aapki delivery penalties aur overtime cost par kya asar padega?" SPIN model mein ye kis type ka question hai?
questions.explanation: Problem (breakdowns) pehle se pata hai; ye question us problem ke business consequences (penalties, overtime) explore karta hai, isliye implication question, option B. Option D trap hai: problem question pain point dhoondhta hai ("kya machines achaanak band hoti hain?"). Need-payoff (option C) solution ki value poochhta hai ("breakdowns aadhe ho jaayein to kitna bachega?").

questions.question: Fictional packaging supplier 'Patra Packs' ke ek B2B account se har saal ₹3 lakh margin aata hai. Pehle saal ka margin pakka hai; uske baad har saal account bane rehne ki probability 80% hai (pichhle saal account tha to). Discounting ignore karke is account ka expected total margin kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Expected margin = 3 × (1 + 0.8 + 0.8² + ...) = 3 ÷ (1 − 0.8) = ₹15 lakh, option C (expected relationship 5 saal). Option B (3 × 0.8 ÷ 0.2) pehle saal ke pakke margin ko chhod deta hai. Option D (3 ÷ 0.8) retention ko galat jagah lagata hai, aur option A sirf doosre saal ka expected margin (3 × 0.8) hai.

weeks.title: Spreadsheets for Analysts: References, Lookups, Conditional Sums and Pivots
weeks.summary: Is week aap Excel mein relative/absolute references, IF, COUNTIF(S)/SUMIF(S), VLOOKUP aur INDEX/MATCH, pivot tables aur basic data cleaning ko business sales data par use karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Cell references**: `A1` relative hai: formula copy karne par row aur column dono shift hote hain. `$A$1` absolute: kuch nahi badalta (tax rate, exchange rate jaisi fixed cell ke liye). Mixed: `$A1` mein column lock, row chalti hai; `A$1` mein row lock, column chalta hai. Formula ko B2 se D4 copy karo to har relative part 2 column aur 2 row shift hota hai.

**IF aur logical tests**: `=IF(test, value_if_true, value_if_false)`. Nested IF upar se neeche check hota hai, isliye slabs mein badi condition pehle likho. `AND()`/`OR()` test ke andar use hote hain, jaise `=IF(AND(D2>=100, E2="Paid"), "Bonus", "")`.

**Conditional aggregation**: `COUNTIF(range, criteria)`, `SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range)`, aur multiple conditions ke liye `COUNTIFS`/`SUMIFS`/`AVERAGEIF`. Dhyaan do: `SUMIFS` mein sum_range PEHLE aata hai, `SUMIF` mein aakhri. Operator wale criteria quotes mein: `">=500"`; cell se jodne ke liye `">="&G1`. Wildcards: `*` (koi bhi characters), `?` (ek character). Text matching case-insensitive hai.

**VLOOKUP**: `=VLOOKUP(key, table, col_index, FALSE)` key ko table ke pehle (leftmost) column mein dhoondhta hai aur usi row ka col_index-th column (table ke start se gina hua) lautata hai. FALSE = exact match, pehla match milta hai, na mile to `#N/A`. TRUE ya chautha argument chhod dena = approximate match: first column ascending sorted hona chahiye aur woh key se chhota-ya-barabar sabse bada value pakadta hai; discount ya tax slabs ke liye yahi chahiye.

**INDEX/MATCH**: `MATCH(key, range, 0)` exact match ki position (range ke andar) deta hai; `INDEX(range, row_num, col_num)` us position ki value. Saath mein: `=INDEX(B2:B100, MATCH(G1, D2:D100, 0))`. Fayde: key column left mein hona zaroori nahi, aur beech mein column insert karne par formula nahi tootta.

**Pivot tables**: source data ek clean table honi chahiye: ek header row, har column ek field, koi blank row ya merged cell nahi. Fields ko Rows, Columns, Values aur Filters mein daalo. Numeric field default Sum leta hai, text field Count. Source data badalne par pivot ko **Refresh** karna padta hai. Pivot ka 'Average' raw rows se nikalta hai, isliye woh sahi weighted average hai.

**Data cleaning**: `TRIM()` extra spaces hataata hai ('North ' aur 'North' alag keys hain, lookup `#N/A` dega). Numbers jo text ki tarah store hain, unhe `SUM` range mein ignore karta hai, isliye total chupke se kam aata hai. Remove Duplicates, consistent category labels, aur dates ko proper date format mein rakhna pivot se pehle zaroori hai.

example.problem: Fictional 'Saraswati Stationers' ki sales sheet (code dekho) mein: (a) North region ke Notebooks ka total amount, (b) ₹6,000 ya usse bade orders ki ginti, aur (c) Region-wise total amount ka pivot nikaalo.
steps: (a) Do conditions hain, isliye SUMIFS: `=SUMIFS(E2:E9, B2:B9, "North", C2:C9, "Notebooks")`. Sirf row 4 (O103) match karti hai, result 6000.
(b) `=COUNTIF(E2:E9, ">=6000")`: 6000, 9600, 6000, 10000, 8400 count hote hain, result 5. `">6000"` likhte to dono 6000 chhoot jaate aur 3 aata.
(c) Insert → PivotTable, Region ko Rows mein aur Amount ko Values mein (Sum of Amount) daalo.
Pivot result: East 18400, North 15200, South 18900; Grand Total 52500.
Check: 18400 + 15200 + 18900 = 52500 = `SUM(E2:E9)`; ye cross-check har pivot ke baad karo.
example.code:
A      B       C          D     E
1    Order  Region  Product    Qty   Amount
2    O101   North   Pens       120   6000
3    O102   South   Notebooks  80    9600
4    O103   North   Notebooks  50    6000
5    O104   East    Pens       200   10000
6    O105   South   Pens       90    4500
7    O106   North   Files      40    3200
8    O107   East    Notebooks  70    8400
9    O108   South   Files      60    4800

=SUMIFS(E2:E9, B2:B9, "North", C2:C9, "Notebooks")   -> 6000
=COUNTIF(E2:E9, ">=6000")                           -> 5

mistakes: VLOOKUP ka chautha argument chhod dena. Default approximate match hai, jo unsorted ID column par bina error ke galat row utha leta hai. ID lookup mein hamesha FALSE (ya 0) likho.
Formula copy karne se pehle `$` lagana bhool jaana, jisse tax-rate cell bhi shift ho jaati hai. Pehle socho kaunsa part fixed hai, phir F4 se lock karo.

Region-wise averages ka simple average lekar 'overall average' bana dena. Agar regions mein orders ki sankhya alag hai to overall average = total amount ÷ total orders (pivot ka Grand Total average) hota hai.
revision: `$A$1` fixed, `$A1` column fixed, `A$1` row fixed.
`SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range)` vs `SUMIFS(sum_range, range1, criteria1, ...)`.
VLOOKUP FALSE = exact, pehla match; TRUE = sorted slabs, chhota-ya-barabar sabse bada.
`INDEX(range, MATCH(key, keyrange, 0))` left lookup bhi kar leta hai.
Pivot: clean table, Sum vs Count, data badle to Refresh.
`TRIM` se spaces hatao; text-numbers SUM mein ignore hote hain.

questions.question: Cell E1 mein GST rate hai. Cell C2 mein formula `=B2*$E$1` hai. Is formula ko C2 se C5 tak neeche copy kiya jaata hai. C5 mein formula kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Neeche 3 rows copy karne par relative reference B2 badal kar B5 ho jaata hai, jabki `$E$1` absolute hai aur fixed rehta hai: `=B5*$E$1`, option D. Option A wahi hota jo `$` na lagane par hota (E1 bhi shift ho kar E4). Option C ye sochne ka trap hai ki `$` ke baad bhi row shift hoti hai.

questions.question: Range B2:B8 mein order values hain: 450, 1200, 500, 75, 980, 500, 620. `=COUNTIF(B2:B8, ">=500")` kya return karega?
questions.explanation: 500 ya usse bade values: 1200, 500, 980, 500, 620, yaani 5, option B. COUNTIF har cell alag ginta hai, isliye dono 500 count hote hain; unhe ek baar ginne se option C (4) aata hai. Option A (3) `">500"` ka result hai, jahan boundary value chhoot jaati hai.

questions.question: Ek price-volume grid mein cell B2 ka formula `=$A2*B$1` hai (column A mein quantities, row 1 mein prices). Is formula ko B2 se D4 par copy kiya jaata hai. D4 mein formula kya hoga?
questions.explanation: B2 se D4 = 2 column right, 2 row neeche. `$A2` mein column A locked hai, row chalti hai: `$A4`. `B$1` mein row 1 locked hai, column chalta hai: `D$1`. Result `=$A4*D$1`, option C. Option A row shift bhool jaata hai, option D column shift; option B `$` ko ignore karke sab kuch shift kar deta hai.

questions.question: Fictional distributor ki discount slab table G2:H5 mein ascending order mein hai (code dekho). Order value ₹30,000 ke liye `=VLOOKUP(30000, G2:H5, 2, TRUE)` kya dega?
questions.explanation: TRUE = approximate match: sorted column G mein 30000 se chhota-ya-barabar sabse bada value 25000 hai, isliye us row ka 8% milta hai, option A. Option B ye sochne ka trap hai ki agla (bada) slab uthta hai. Option C exact match (FALSE) ka result hota, kyunki 30000 table mein nahi hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Disha Electricals' ki sheet (code dekho) par `=SUMIFS(D2:D9, B2:B9, "West", D2:D9, ">5000")` kya return karega?
questions.code:
A      B       C       D
1    Order  Region  Rep     Amount
2    S01    West    Kiran   7200
3    S02    East    Lata    5400
4    S03    West    Mohan   4800
5    S04    West    Kiran   5000
6    S05    North   Lata    9100
7    S06    West    Mohan   6300
8    S07    East    Kiran   8000
9    S08    West    Lata    5600
questions.explanation: Dono conditions ek saath: Region West AUR Amount > 5000. West rows: 7200, 4800, 5000, 6300, 5600; inme > 5000: 7200 + 6300 + 5600 = 19100, option C. Option B 5000 ko bhi gin leta hai (`">=5000"` jaisa). Option A sirf West condition lagata hai, aur option D sirf amount condition.

questions.question: Neeche di gayi sheet par `=INDEX(B2:D6, MATCH(MAX(D2:D6), D2:D6, 0), 2)` kya return karega?
questions.code:
A      B       C       D
1    EmpID  Name    Region  Sales
2    E101   Asha    North   42000
3    E102   Bilal   South   58000
4    E103   Charu   East    58000
5    E104   Dev     North   31000
6    E105   Esha    West    47000
questions.explanation: MAX(D2:D6) = 58000. MATCH(..., 0) exact match ki PEHLI position deta hai: D2:D6 mein 58000 pehli baar position 2 (row 3) par hai. INDEX(B2:D6, 2, 2) = range B:D ka doosra column (C) aur doosri row: 'South', option B. Option A column ko B ke bajaay A se ginne ka trap hai, option C ye sochna ki aakhri match (Charu) uthega, aur option D column 3 lene ki galti.
